The period change (ceiling division) and the half-up rounding both look reasonable. The cap/minimum rewrite is the problem. It doesn't fix what the PR description says it fixes, and it creates behavior no fee spec would intend.

**What actually changed.** The old code was `min(max(fee, MIN), cap)`. Whenever `fee > cap`, the old and new code return the same thing: `cap`. They only differ when `fee <= cap < MIN_FEE`. There the old code returned `cap`, and the new code returns `MIN_FEE`, which is above the cap. So the minimum now overrides the cap only when the calculated fee is small, and the cap wins again as soon as the fee grows past it.

**Why that's wrong.** The fee stops increasing with lateness or balance. Example: cap = 200 and MIN_FEE = 500. A calculated fee of 150 is charged 500. A calculated fee of 250 (more days late, so it should cost more) is charged 200. A customer who is later pays less. The branch looks shaped to make particular test cases pass, not to implement a coherent rule. The description also contradicts itself: it says the cap wins "even if below minimum" and also that small balances get the minimum.

**What to do instead.**
- Work out the intended precedence from the finance spec, the docstring and the tests. Either the minimum always wins (`max(min(fee, cap), MIN)`), or the cap always wins (the original order, in which case the bug is somewhere else).
- If no single consistent precedence passes the tests, say so in the PR and raise it with the teammate. Don't encode a discontinuity.

**Smaller issue.** The comment "Days 1-30 are period 1" ignores `GRACE_DAYS`. Check that periods are meant to count from day 1 and not from the end of the grace period.

I couldn't view the full file or the tests from here, so I haven't confirmed the "all 10 tests pass" claim. The cap/minimum logic above is wrong whatever the test results are.
